title: How Farza and Sharif jumpstarted Tidbit in 14 days in Japan
summary: Farza recounts finding a co-founder in Sharif after five years solo, then flying to Tokyo with no idea to build. Daily prototypes, one-liner tweets, demo-driven development and rapid user calls turned into a product with paying customers and 1000+ DMs in two weeks.

principles.text: Try stuff to find stuff: build aggressively with no fixed plan and let experiments reveal the product.
principles.quote: Both me and Sharif have the same philosophies when it comes to building stuff — you gotta try stuff to find stuff.

principles.text: Test product vision by writing one-liners and launch tweets; if you both find it exciting, you're aligned.
principles.quote: if we could describe the idea in one line or make it sound exciting in a tweet — then we’d be on the same page.

principles.text: Run a tight daily loop: plan in a 30-60 minute morning check-in, ship by evening, and surface co-founder friction immediately.
principles.quote: Every morning around 9AM we’d spend 30-60 minutes to figure out what we wanted to do by 9PM.

principles.text: Make the goal a product you love using yourself, and optimize for learnings rather than vanity metrics.
principles.quote: We were optimizing for learnings. Not a user number, or a graph, or a money number.

principles.text: Ship demos daily and shamelessly, without polish; demos force clarity and attract the first real signal.
principles.quote: We also agree to start posting daily demos immediately. We were gonna be shameless. Didn’t care about polish.

principles.text: Talk to users to learn why they're excited; unexpected use cases from them shape the product for you.
principles.quote: My main goal of the convos was to get a clearer and clearer idea of why people were excited about it.
